tier: 0 (ADR-0091) — no run; the six existing planner transcripts re-priced
instrument: scripts/planner-dollars.py; rates: Anthropic first-party list prices as cached by the claude-api reference on 25 Sep 2026 (Opus 5.5 $4/$20, cache read $0.20; Opus 5 $5/$25, $0.50; 5-minute cache writes 1.25x input)
findings: Cache reads are the largest dollar term (33–67 % of each planner's bill); output, thinking included, is 19–38 %. The token metric P_total excluded cache reads, so it was blind to the largest dollar cost. The lever is fewer and shorter turns, not less thinking.
Planning dollars per planned task, as a pass launched alone pays: $0.22–0.30 at N ≈ 11 and $0.074–0.077 at N ≈ 36–45 on Opus 5.5.
Opus 5 (20 Sep) → Opus 5.5 (25 Sep) roughly halved the dollars of comparable passes; model price moves as much as design does.

comparator_estimate.basis: Phase 11b arm A (Opus alone, one fresh session per task): a ~47.9k-token session floor plus 2.8–6.0k tokens per task (experiments/status-quo/results/arm-a-project-a-tokens.json). Token classes were not split, so dollars are a rough reading only.
comparator_estimate.reading: If Opus alone did a batch in one session, it pays the floor once and ~3–6k tokens per task of mostly output and context. At Opus 5.5 rates that is of the same order as sidecrew's planning alone at N ≈ 40 ($0.07–0.08 per task) — before counting that sidecrew's workers and gate are free and Opus-alone's reads, edits and test runs are not. The 50 % claim cannot be assessed until an Opus-alone batch arm is measured with its token classes; that arm is the missing instrument (ADR-0093).
